newsitem.title: KENYA: T-Bill rates down again at Kenyan auction.
newsitem.headline: T-Bill rates down again at Kenyan auction.

text.p: Treasury bill rates continued on a downward trend at the latest Kenyan auction this week as the Central Bank of Kenya pressed on with iits efforts to gradually cut interest rates, central bank officials said on Friday.

The Central Bank of Kenya said that about 4.489 billion shillings of the 5.0 billion shillings it tendered was accepted. An official said investors were becoming "reasonable" as they realised the bank would not offer "ridiculous" rates.
The auction is held late on Thursdays.
On its main 91-day category of treasury bills, the bank offered an average interest rate of 22.150 percent, marginally lower compared to 22.497 percent in the previous week.
The bank offered an unchanged 15.005 percent rate for its 28-day category of treasury bills.

The bank accepted 29.75 million shillings in 28-day bills and around 4.459 billion shillings in 91-day bills. Some 300,000 shillings in 182-day bills was also accepted but the bank did not say what interest rate it offered for that.

"As you can see, the rates are coming down steadily. We are doing everything to contain a persistent surge in interest rates," a senior bank official told Reuters. "This direction has become quite obvious for the moment."
The bank invited tenders for treasury bills of 10 billion shillings for the next week to be submitted by Thursday.
Commercial bank lending rates currently range in the 24-30 percent range. Interest on deposits is around 10-16 percent.
